patient.chief_complaint: Witnessed cardiac arrest resuscitated, now unresponsive — EEG shows burst-suppression, unsure if NCSE or post-anoxic sedation
patient.hpi: A 62-year-old retired firefighter was brought to the emergency department after witnessed cardiac arrest at a gym. Bystanders initiated CPR immediately. EMS arrived 7 minutes after collapse. The patient was found in ventricular fibrillation; two defibrillation shocks achieved ROSC after approximately 11 minutes of cardiac arrest. He arrived intubated with propofol 10 mcg/kg/min infusion for sedation. He is now in the ICU for targeted temperature management (TTM at 36°C). EEG was ordered by the on-call neurology resident due to concern about 'subtle limb movements' observed by nursing — periodic flexion of the left arm and subtle left facial twitching. The night team is unsure whether these movements are (A) myoclonic status epilepticus post-anoxia (malignant, poor prognosis), (B) NCSE from another cause, or (C) post-anoxic myoclonus without EEG correlate (sometimes benign, as in action myoclonus-renal failure syndrome, or sometimes malignant Lance-Adams syndrome). The patient's wife reports he had a recent syncopal episode 2 weeks ago that was worked up and 'told it was benign.' He takes metoprolol and aspirin for coronary artery disease. His cardiologist called and reports he is on amiodarone loading post-arrest. No prior epilepsy.

past_medical_history: Coronary artery disease — 3-vessel disease, prior CABG 8 years ago
Prior syncopal episode 2 weeks ago — evaluated, 'benign' per wife
No prior epilepsy or neurological disease

eeg.impression: DIAGNOSTICALLY AMBIGUOUS BURST-SUPPRESSION. Preserved EEG reactivity to stimulation is a favorable prognostic sign. Clinical correlation recommended.

labs.interpretation: Abnormal values: WBC 11.2 x10^9/L (H), Glucose 168 mg/dL (H), Troponin I (high-sensitivity) 12.8 ng/mL (H), BNP 2840 pg/mL (H), NSE (neuron-specific enolase) 18 mcg/L (H).

ct.impression: Diffuse cerebral edema from post-anoxic hypoxic-ischemic encephalopathy. No hemorrhage. CT underestimates anoxic injury — MRI DWI required after TTM completion for prognostication.
recommended_actions: MRI brain with DWI after TTM completion
Reduce propofol before interpreting EEG burst-suppression

output.impression: Post-anoxic myoclonic status epilepticus (MSE) confirmed: burst-suppression persists after sedation reduction; left arm jerking is electroclinically correlated. Loss of EEG reactivity at 4 hours is an additional poor prognostic sign. Note: treating post-anoxic MSE aggressively (e.g., burst-suppression induction with propofol/midazolam) has NOT been shown to improve outcomes. AED (levetiracetam) may be given but prognosis discussion with family is the priority. Clinical correlation recommended.

interactions.description: Amiodarone + lacosamide: additive sodium channel blockade causing PR prolongation, AV block, and bradycardia. Amiodarone loading dose (150 mg bolus + 1 mg/min infusion) already prolongs PR to 240 ms. Adding lacosamide can cause complete heart block in this compromised post-arrest heart.
interactions.clinical_recommendation: AVOID lacosamide in patient on amiodarone loading. Use levetiracetam as AED of choice for post-anoxic SE.

interactions.description: Amiodarone + levetiracetam: no pharmacokinetic or pharmacodynamic interaction. Levetiracetam has no sodium/calcium channel effects.
interactions.clinical_recommendation: Levetiracetam is the safe AED choice in post-cardiac arrest patient on amiodarone.

output.summary: Amiodarone loading + lacosamide = major cardiac conduction risk (AV block). Use levetiracetam. Monitor ECG closely throughout management.

output.methodology: Bilateral median nerve stimulation at 56h post-arrest after propofol reduced
output.impression: Bilateral absent N20 SSEP responses at 56 hours post-arrest after sedation reduction. Combined with post-anoxic MSE on EEG and early NSE elevation trending upward, this indicates very poor neurological prognosis (near 100% specificity for death or persistent vegetative state per AAN guidelines).
recommended_actions: Urgent family meeting — goals of care

output.impression: Extensive diffuse hypoxic-ischemic encephalopathy — nearly total cortical involvement. This MRI pattern at 48h post-arrest with bilateral absent SSEPs and post-anoxic MSE on EEG is associated with essentially 100% poor neurological outcome. Clinical correlation recommended.

output.interpretation: Abnormal values: NSE at 24h post-arrest 18 mcg/L (H), NSE at 48h post-arrest 68 mcg/L (H), NSE at 72h post-arrest 82 mcg/L (H).
abnormal_values_summary: NSE 82 mcg/L at 72h (markedly elevated, rising) — very poor prognosis

results.title: Post-anoxic status epilepticus: treatment and prognosis
results.key_finding: Post-anoxic MSE with burst-suppression and bilateral absent SSEPs: AED treatment (levetiracetam, valproate) may reduce seizure burden but does NOT improve neurological outcome. Aggressive treatment with anesthetic agents (propofol/midazolam titration to burst-suppression) is not recommended — does not improve survival or neurological function. Prognosis discussion with family is the priority. Avoid AED escalation beyond levetiracetam as it prolongs ICU stay without benefit.

output.summary: Post-anoxic MSE: treat symptomatically with levetiracetam but do NOT escalate to anesthetic doses. Multimodal prognostication (EEG + MRI + SSEP + NSE) guides goals-of-care discussion. Aggressive treatment does not improve outcomes in post-anoxic MSE with multiple poor prognostic markers.

ground_truth.primary_diagnosis: Post-anoxic myoclonic status epilepticus (MSE) with burst-suppression EEG after out-of-hospital cardiac arrest, presenting diagnostic challenge from concurrent propofol sedation and hypothermia masking EEG interpretation

differential.key_features: Propofol causes dose-dependent burst-suppression; KEY TEST: reduce propofol and repeat EEG — if burst-suppression resolves, it was drug-induced; if persists (as in this case), post-anoxic MSE confirmed
TTM at 36°C (not 33°C) — mild hypothermia rarely causes burst-suppression alone; propofol is more likely contributor; burst-suppression at 36°C suggests post-anoxic injury

differential.diagnosis: Focal NCSE (from treatable cause — autoimmune, metabolic)
differential.key_features: Post-anoxic pattern with diffuse cortical involvement; autoimmune panel negative; no focal lesion; MRI shows diffuse HIE pattern

optimal_actions.action: Urgent EEG to characterize burst-suppression pattern
optimal_actions.expected_finding: Burst-suppression with left hemisphere spike activity correlating with left arm jerking

optimal_actions.action: REDUCE propofol (10 to 5 mcg/kg/min) and repeat EEG in 30-60 minutes — critical step to distinguish drug-induced vs post-anoxic burst-suppression
optimal_actions.expected_finding: Burst-suppression persists after reduction = post-anoxic MSE confirmed

optimal_actions.action: Check drug interactions: amiodarone + AED choice — lacosamide contraindicated, use levetiracetam
optimal_actions.expected_finding: Amiodarone + lacosamide = AV block risk; levetiracetam is safe

optimal_actions.action: IV levetiracetam 1500 mg loading (symptomatic treatment for post-anoxic MSE) — NOT expected to improve prognosis
optimal_actions.expected_finding: Possible mild reduction in myoclonic burden — prognosis unchanged

optimal_actions.action: Serial NSE at 48h and 72h post-arrest for prognostication
optimal_actions.expected_finding: NSE >33 mcg/L at 48h (68) and rising at 72h (82) — very poor prognosis

optimal_actions.action: SSEP after propofol reduction at 48-72h post-arrest
optimal_actions.expected_finding: Bilateral absent N20 — 100% specific for poor outcome

optimal_actions.action: MRI brain DWI after TTM completion (48-72h) for extent of injury
optimal_actions.expected_finding: Extensive bilateral cortical DWI restriction — maximal HIE pattern

optimal_actions.action: Goals-of-care family meeting with neurology, cardiology, palliative care after multimodal prognostication complete
optimal_actions.expected_finding: Informed family decision based on poor prognosis markers

critical_actions: Reduce propofol and repeat EEG — cannot interpret burst-suppression without excluding drug-induced artifact
Levetiracetam preferred AED — amiodarone loading precludes lacosamide (PR prolongation/AV block)
Serial NSE at 48h and 72h — prognostication requires delayed measurement, not <24h
Bilateral SSEPs after sedation reduction — most reliable predictor of outcome
Multimodal prognostication before any withdrawal of care decision
contraindicated_actions: Lacosamide in patient on amiodarone loading — additive sodium channel blockade causing AV block
Aggressive burst-suppression induction (propofol/midazolam dose escalation) for post-anoxic MSE — does NOT improve outcomes; prolongs ICU stay without benefit
Prognosticating <24h — early NSE, early EEG findings unreliable; sedation confounds all early results
Withdrawing care without completing multimodal prognostication
key_reasoning_points: Burst-suppression interpretation requires distinguishing drug-induced (propofol/hypothermia) from post-anoxic — the CRITICAL step is sedation reduction trial with repeat EEG
Amiodarone loading + lacosamide = major interaction: both affect sodium channels causing additive PR/QRS prolongation and AV block risk in compromised post-arrest heart
Post-anoxic MSE: AED treatment (levetiracetam) may be given but does NOT improve neurological outcomes — prognosis discussion is the priority
Neuroprognostication requires minimum 72h post-arrest after TTM completion: NSE at 48-72h, SSEPs after sedation reduction, MRI DWI, EEG pattern
Rising NSE trend (18 → 68 → 82 over 72h) = ongoing neuronal destruction = actively deteriorating HIE

red_herrings.data_point: Propofol 10 mcg/kg/min infusion noted in medications
red_herrings.intended_effect: Suggest burst-suppression is entirely propofol-induced, leading to under-treatment of post-anoxic MSE
red_herrings.correct_interpretation: Propofol can cause burst-suppression; however, sedation reduction trial shows burst-suppression persists — post-anoxic MSE is the primary cause. Propofol contributes but is not the sole explanation.

red_herrings.data_point: Mild EEG reactivity to stimulation on initial EEG
red_herrings.intended_effect: Suggest preserved cortical function and reasonable prognosis, potentially delaying goals-of-care discussion
red_herrings.correct_interpretation: Initial EEG reactivity is a favorable sign but must be interpreted with full multimodal assessment. EEG reactivity was lost at 4 hours — progressive deterioration. Bilateral absent SSEPs + rising NSE + extensive DWI restriction override initial reactivity sign.

metadata.teaching_points: Propofol vs post-anoxic burst-suppression; sedation reduction trial; amiodarone + lacosamide AV block; NSE prognostication timing; multimodal prognosis before withdrawal
metadata.pitfalls: Not reducing propofol before interpreting burst-suppression; lacosamide in amiodarone patient; premature prognostication; aggressive AED escalation in post-anoxic MSE
metadata.clinical_pearl: Burst-suppression on EEG + propofol: ALWAYS reduce sedation and repeat EEG first. Amiodarone loading = no lacosamide. Post-anoxic MSE prognosis = multimodal assessment at 48-72h.
